## Total Household Resources

Total household resources are the total income (taxable and nontaxable) of both spouses or of a single person maintaining a household. ## Health Insurance Premiums

Line 31 requires you to enter health insurance premiums, Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) premiums, or other insurance premiums you paid for yourself and your family. This includes medical insurance and dental insurance.

## 23% Rent for Renters

In most cases, 23 percent of rent paid is considered property tax that can be claimed for credit. This applies to renters claiming the homestead property tax credit on the MI-1040CR form.

Based on the web search results, I found the information you're looking for regarding Michigan's homestead property tax credit and employer-paid health insurance premiums.

Premiums paid by an employer with pre-tax contributions are not deductible when calculating total household resources for the Michigan homestead property tax credit. This is specifically listed under "PREMIUMS NOT DEDUCTIBLE FROM TOTAL HOUSEHOLD RESOURCES."

In contrast, post-tax premiums paid for medical insurance (including self-employed) and dental insurance may be deducted to compute applicable credits.

The distinction is important: while total household resources includes all income received by all household members during the year, including income that might be exempt from adjusted gross income, employer-paid pre-tax health insurance premiums must be included in total household resources and cannot be deducted when determining eligibility or calculating the credit amount.
